# Native Structural Weld Admission

This provisional F07 software slice admits one exact structural component in
the constrained-muscle replay policy: a native `WeldJoint` with zero
coordinates and valid, distinct parent and child physical frames. The
`WeldJoint` itself must pass OpenSim's native concrete-class cast. Frame
references must resolve to reviewed `Body`, `Ground`, or
`PhysicalOffsetFrame` components and carry absolute component paths. The
source model hash binds socket selection and all serialized frame transforms.

This admission is separate from the strict base muscle-bundle component set;
that set remains unchanged. `WeldConstraint`, plugin or substitute classes,
controllers, prescribed motion, and undeclared non-muscle forces remain
rejected. A weld does not waive state, constraint, force, wrapped-path,
contact, or native initialization checks.

The synthetic fixture for issue #12280 uses nonzero weld-frame translation
and rotation, attaches a muscle path to the welded body, and retains movable
and coupled coordinates. The selected native fixture run passed all three
cases: fresh reload and saved-excitation replay, plus source-mutation
rejections for a weld-frame orientation and parent-frame socket. The pure
admission tests remain a separate 14-case check. Raw public test outputs and
their hashes are archived under
`docs/development/feedback_controls/evidence/native_weldjoint_12280/`.

This synthetic result establishes only this software path. It does not
establish capture matching, anatomy, support or grip, physiological validity,
full-clock replay, or qualification of a production model. The aggregate
pre-PR check remains incomplete: its first run reported duplicate mypy module
identities and missing vendor initialization, and the bounded mypy retry was
stopped at the local resource cap before producing a result. The calculation
registry remains release-blocked.
